records.subject: DocBrain
records.claim: docbrain-ai/docbrain exists: self-hosted knowledge system capturing decisions from agent sessions, PRs, chat, incidents and deploys and serving them with citations; re-checks claims against sources for freshness; signed offline-verifiable .dbev evidence bundles; MCP server. Rust + PostgreSQL + OpenSearch + Redis. Repo MIT; server binaries BSL 1.1.
records.reproducibility: Self-hostable.
records.relevance: Comparable system to TRACE evidence model
records.limitations: Feature claims self-reported; 33 stars.

records.subject: KnowledgeDrift
records.claim: techtheist/knowledgedrift exists (MIT, 14 stars): offline benchmark for AI memory systems on seeded fictional project notes, with no LLM judge; 8 task families (retrieval, abstention, currency, contradiction, drift, deletion, rationale, temporal); 1,000-point score. README reports reference system Engram 0.9.9 at 800 and TF-IDF baseline at 580.
records.reproducibility: Frozen seeded worlds; designed to be reproducible.
records.limitations: Scores self-reported by the author.
records.nextAction: Run harness locally before citing scores.

records.subject: AgentPoison
records.claim: AgentPoison (Chen et al., arXiv 2407.12784) backdoors LLM agents by poisoning long-term memory or RAG knowledge bases with optimized triggers; reports >80% average attack success at <0.1% poison rate.
records.reproducibility: Code referenced by paper.
records.limitations: Trigger-based.

records.subject: PoisonedRAG
records.claim: PoisonedRAG (Zou et al., arXiv 2402.07867; USENIX Security 2025) injects a few texts into a RAG knowledge base to force attacker-chosen answers (about 90% success with five texts per target).
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: RAG rather than agent memory.

records.subject: MINJA
records.claim: MINJA (Dong et al., arXiv 2503.03704) plants malicious records into an agent's memory using only queries and observed outputs, so later victim queries retrieve them.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: None

records.subject: MemoryGraft
records.claim: MemoryGraft (Srivastava and He, arXiv 2512.16962) plants fabricated 'successful' experiences in long-term memory so agents imitate unsafe procedures later.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Preprint.

records.subject: MINJA under realistic memory
records.claim: Sunil et al. (arXiv 2601.05504) find MINJA success drops sharply when memory already holds benign records (GPT-4o-mini about 62% to 6.7% with six prior memories) and rises with more retrieved memories; their trust-scored sanitization was poorly calibrated across models.
records.reproducibility: EHR agent on MIMIC-III.
records.limitations: Single domain, preprint.

records.subject: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
records.claim: OWASP GenAI Security Project published the Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026 edition) in December 2025; secondary sources label ASI06 'Memory and Context Poisoning', with mitigations such as write validation, memory segmentation, trust decay and rollback.
records.evidence: Search results for OWASP pages; ASI06 wording from secondary sources.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Official PDF not read.
records.nextAction: Read OWASP document for exact ASI06 text.

records.subject: pass@k
records.claim: pass@k (Chen et al., 'Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code', arXiv 2107.03374) is the chance at least one of k samples passes; unbiased estimator 1 - E[C(n-c,k)/C(n,k)].
records.evidence: Formula restated in tau-bench paper (fetched); Codex abstract fetched.
records.reproducibility: Formula.
records.limitations: Rewards lucky successes.

records.subject: pass^k
records.claim: pass^k (tau-bench, Yao et al., arXiv 2406.12045) is the chance that all k i.i.d. trials succeed, averaged over tasks; estimator E[C(c,k)/C(n,k)]. It measures reliability rather than best-of-k capability.
records.reproducibility: Formula.
records.limitations: Requires n >= k trials per task.

records.subject: tau-bench reliability result
records.claim: tau-bench reported top function-calling agents below 25% pass^8 in the retail domain (June 2024 models and harness).
records.reproducibility: Benchmark public.
records.limitations: 2024 models; superseded results likely exist.

records.subject: Agent Zero Memory (provenance-aware)
records.claim: Wu and Zhu (arXiv 2608.29606) propose long-term agent memory where items carry origin category, timestamp and pointer to source artifacts, with answers restricted to cited items; report results on LongMemEval and LoCoMo.
records.reproducibility: Benchmarks public.
records.limitations: Preprint, unreviewed; benchmark results self-reported.

records.subject: Ground Truth First
records.claim: Spencer (arXiv 2607.21962) generates agent-memory benchmarks from a fact script so answer keys are correct by construction, and reports memory-architecture rankings reversing as history lengthens.
records.reproducibility: Method designed for reproducibility.
records.limitations: Preprint, single author.

records.subject: Veracium
records.claim: Veracium (PyPI 0.4.x) describes itself as a provenance-aware memory plug-in recording who asserted each claim and keeping prior values as history.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Not fetched.

records.subject: W3C PROV
records.claim: W3C PROV is a family of 12 documents (Working Group Note overview dated 2013-04-30), with PROV-DM, PROV-O, PROV-N and PROV-CONSTRAINTS as Recommendations, describing provenance in terms of entities, activities and the people involved.
records.reproducibility: Standard.
records.relevance: Provenance vocabulary for TRACE memory records
records.limitations: None

records.subject: pytest JUnit XML
records.claim: pytest writes JUnit XML with --junit-xml=path (documented for CI servers), configurable via junit_suite_name and junit_duration_report; current docs show no built-in JSON report.
records.reproducibility: Built-in.
records.limitations: junit_family not mentioned on this page.

records.subject: pytest-json-report plugin
records.claim: JSON output needs a plugin such as pytest-json-report (--json-report, --json-report-file); latest release 1.5.0 on 2022-03-15, '4 - Beta' status.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: No release for 4+ years; maintenance uncertain.
records.nextAction: Prefer JUnit XML as primary artefact.

records.subject: Stryker mutation testing
records.claim: Stryker mutates production code and reruns tests; platforms are StrykerJS (JS/TS), Stryker.NET (C#) and Stryker4s (Scala). A killed mutant fails at least one test; a survived mutant indicates a missing test.
records.reproducibility: Deterministic given seed/config.
records.limitations: None

records.subject: Stryker mutant states and score
records.claim: States: Pending, Killed, Survived, No coverage, Timeout, Runtime error, Compile error, Ignored. Mutation score = detected / valid x 100, detected = killed + timeout, undetected = survived + no coverage; errors and ignored are excluded.
records.reproducibility: Formula deterministic.
records.limitations: None

records.subject: Vitest JSON reporter
records.claim: Vitest's json reporter emits Jest --json-compatible output (numTotalTests, numFailedTests, testResults[].assertionResults), includes coverageMap since Vitest 3, defaults to .vitest/json/output.json and honours outputFile.
records.reproducibility: Built-in.
records.limitations: Default path stated for v5 docs; earlier versions differ.

records.subject: Vitest JUnit reporter
records.claim: junit reporter writes JUnit XML (default .vitest/junit/output.xml) with templates for suite/class/title names; {filename} is the project-relative path, unlike jest-junit.
records.reproducibility: Built-in.
records.limitations: None

records.subject: git worktree
records.claim: git worktree add creates linked worktrees sharing one repository; HEAD and index are per-worktree; lock, prune, remove and unlock manage lifecycle; remove requires a clean tree unless --force.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: None

records.subject: git worktree isolation limits
records.claim: All refs/ are shared except refs/bisect, refs/worktree and refs/rewritten; config is shared unless extensions.worktreeConfig is enabled; a branch checked out in one worktree is refused in another without --force. Worktrees isolate files, index and HEAD, not repository state.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.relevance: Agents can still clobber shared refs/config
records.limitations: None
records.nextAction: Combine with per-agent branches and no shared config writes.

records.subject: Aider polyglot benchmark
records.claim: 225 Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust, selected from 697 as those solved by three or fewer of seven top models; replaced the saturated 133-exercise Python benchmark (2024-12-21).
records.reproducibility: Exercises public.
records.limitations: Exercism solutions are widely public (contamination risk); selection depends on 2024 models.

records.subject: Aider leaderboard
records.claim: Leaderboard reports percent correct (second attempt as headline) and the edit format used; maintained by Paul Gauthier; last updated 2025-11-20.
records.reproducibility: Harness in aider repo.
records.limitations: Almost a year without updates at observation date.

records.subject: Arena (formerly LMArena) URL
records.claim: https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard returns 301 to https://arena.ai/leaderboard, which is the canonical URL; arena.ai returned 403 to automated fetch. Rebrand from LMArena to Arena dated 2026-01-28.
records.evidence: Observed 301 redirect; Wikipedia for rebrand date.
records.reproducibility: Redirect re-checkable.
records.limitations: Content not read.

records.subject: Arena methodology
records.claim: Arena ranks models from crowdsourced, anonymous pairwise human votes (Chiang et al., arXiv 2403.04132) using a Bradley-Terry logistic model; 'style control' (2024-08-29) adds covariates for answer length and markdown so scores reflect substance after style.
records.evidence: Fetched arXiv abstract and LMSYS blog.
records.reproducibility: Vote data partly released; live rankings not reproducible.
records.limitations: Measures user preference, not task correctness.

records.subject: Arena operator
records.claim: Arena is operated by a US company (founders Wei-Lin Chiang, Anastasios Angelopoulos, Ion Stoica); Wikipedia lists a $100M seed (May 2025), $150M Series A (Jan 2026) and $200M Series B (Oct 2026).
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Tertiary source.

records.subject: Arena critique
records.claim: 'The Leaderboard Illusion' (Singh et al., arXiv 2504.20879) reports undisclosed private testing of variants, sampling asymmetries favouring large proprietary providers, and silent deprecations; LMArena published a rebuttal.
records.reproducibility: Analysis based on Arena data.
records.limitations: Disputed by operator.

records.subject: LiveCodeBench
records.claim: LiveCodeBench (Berkeley/MIT/Cornell; arXiv 2403.07974) collects dated problems from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces and evaluates code generation, self-repair, code execution and test-output prediction; contamination is limited by evaluating only on problems released after a model's cutoff.
records.reproducibility: Public problems and runner.
records.limitations: Competitive programming, not repository work.

records.subject: LiveCodeBench releases
records.claim: Repo lists release_v1 (400 problems, to Mar 2024) through release_v6 (1,055 problems, May 2023-Apr 2025); harness lcb_runner computes pass@1 and pass@5.
records.reproducibility: Runner public.
records.limitations: No release after Apr 2025 visible: newer models' cutoffs may overlap the whole window, reducing contamination protection.

records.subject: Luke's Dev Lab site
records.claim: lukesdevlab.com is a model benchmarks page ('Benchmark and agent-test data') for searching and comparing model reports; the landing page states no methodology.
records.reproducibility: Unknown.
records.limitations: Reports load dynamically; methodology not visible.
records.nextAction: Open individual reports to record method.

records.subject: Luke's Dev Lab GitHub
records.claim: github.com/lukesdevlab/youtube exists ('Prompts and model configs used in my videos'); contains model-configs.ini (39 commits, about 280 stars); the file is a llama.cpp/llama-swap-style profile set whose header cites RTX 2000 (16 GB VRAM) + 32 GB DDR4, with quantization, context and sampler settings per model.
records.evidence: Fetched repo page and raw config.
records.reproducibility: Configs public, aiding reproduction; prompts/scoring not seen.
records.limitations: No license shown; single creator.

records.subject: Luke's Dev Lab YouTube channel
records.claim: Channel @lukesdevlab is linked from the GitHub repo; direct fetch redirected to a YouTube consent page, which was not accepted, so channel content was not verified.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Not verified.

records.subject: Harness dependence of scores
records.claim: Agent benchmark scores depend on the scaffold, turn limits, cost caps, trial counts and benchmark version (e.g. Scale mixes 250-turn uncapped and 50-turn capped runs; Terminal-Bench 4.0 is declared non-comparable with 3.0/2.x).
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.relevance: TRACE recording rule: score only with version+harness+date
records.limitations: None

records.subject: SWE-bench (original)
records.claim: SWE-bench: 2,294 task instances from real GitHub issues in 12 Python repositories; a model must produce a patch that resolves the issue as judged by repository tests. Princeton/Stanford authors; ICLR 2024.
records.reproducibility: Dataset public.
records.limitations: Python only; issues pre-date many model cutoffs.

records.subject: SWE-bench harness
records.claim: Evaluation is Docker-based (swebench eval; results in logs/evaluation/<run_id>/results.json); recommended x86_64, 120 GB free disk, 16 GB RAM, 8 cores; sb-cli for cloud evaluation; Multimodal v2 (480 tasks) fully open-sourced 2026-09-01. Site lists Verified, Multimodal, Multilingual, Lite, Full and a Bash Only view.
records.reproducibility: Docker images make grading reproducible; agent runs are stochastic.
records.limitations: No version number on releases.

records.subject: SWE-bench Pro
records.claim: Scale AI benchmark of 1,865 long-horizon tasks from 41 repositories: public set 731 (GPL/copyleft repos), held-out 858 (private), commercial 276 (startup codebases, results only). Copyleft and private sets are the contamination defence.
records.evidence: Fetched arXiv abstract and Scale leaderboard page.
records.reproducibility: Public set reproducible; held-out/commercial are not.
records.limitations: Copyleft licensing deters but does not prevent training exposure.

records.subject: SWE-bench Pro leaderboard methodology
records.claim: Scale's public leaderboard reports resolve rate (fail-to-pass pass and pass-to-pass kept) with confidence intervals; starred entries use the mini-swe-agent harness; most models run uncapped cost with a 250-turn limit, some with capped cost and 50 turns. No update date shown.
records.reproducibility: Scaffold specified; runs stochastic.
records.limitations: Turn/cost caps differ between entries; scores not recorded here because the page shows no date.
records.nextAction: Snapshot with date before citing any score.

records.subject: SWE-bench Verified
records.claim: SWE-bench Verified is a 500-task human-validated subset released by OpenAI with the SWE-bench authors (August 2024).
records.evidence: OpenAI page returned 403; 500-task size confirmed in SWE-bench README.
records.reproducibility: Dataset public.
records.limitations: OpenAI page not fetched.

records.subject: SWE-bench Verified deprecation by OpenAI
records.claim: OpenAI (2026-02-23) stopped reporting SWE-bench Verified, citing increasing contamination and flawed tasks: an audit of 138 tasks o3 could not reliably solve found 59.4% with material test or description problems; OpenAI recommends SWE-bench Pro.
records.evidence: openai.com returned 403 to direct fetch; content from search-engine extract of the OpenAI page and secondary coverage.
records.reproducibility: Audit not independently reproduced.
records.relevance: Do not treat Verified scores as uncontaminated
records.limitations: Not fetched directly.
records.nextAction: Read the OpenAI post in a browser.
records.supersession: Supersedes reliance on SWE-bench Verified as a headline metric

records.subject: SWE-bench Pro grading audit
records.claim: A secondary source reports a May 2026 Datacurve audit finding SWE-bench Pro graders mis-graded roughly a third of trials.
records.evidence: Mentioned in one secondary summary only.
records.reproducibility: Not reproduced.
records.relevance: Pro is not a settled replacement
records.limitations: Primary audit not located.

records.subject: Terminal-Bench
records.claim: Terminal-Bench evaluates agents on end-to-end tasks in sandboxed terminals (compile, train, set up servers); each task has an instruction, test script and reference solution. Hosted by Stanford and the Laude Institute with Harbor; original repo's core set v0.1.1 had about 100 tasks; ICLR 2026 paper.
records.evidence: Fetched site and legacy repo README.
records.reproducibility: Docker tasks with tests; agent runs stochastic.
records.limitations: Legacy repo is superseded by Harbor.

records.subject: Terminal-Bench 4.0
records.claim: tbench.ai homepage shows Terminal-Bench 4.0. Secondary sources: maintenance release (August 2026), 66 tasks after removing 8 and revising ~19-20, 5 trials per task, 8-hour agent timeout, run via 'harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0'; scores not comparable with 3.0 or 2.x.
records.evidence: Version from fetched homepage; details from search extracts of third-party pages.
records.reproducibility: Harbor run command published.
records.limitations: Task counts differ slightly between secondary sources.
records.nextAction: Fetch Harbor Hub dataset card for 4.0.

records.subject: Harbor harness
records.claim: Terminal-Bench is now a 'continuous benchmark' with tagged releases run through Harbor (e.g. harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@latest -k 5 ... --env modal); README asks to run oracle solutions 5x to validate a sandbox.
records.reproducibility: Oracle validation step supports reproducibility.
records.limitations: '@latest' is not a fixed version.

records.subject: canirun.ai
records.claim: canirun.ai is live and ranks open models against detected GPU/Mac hardware with S-F fit grades (S/A/B run, C/D tight, F too heavy).
records.evidence: Fetched landing page shows hardware detection panel, grade legend, model list.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Captured render showed 'detecting...' and '0 of 0 models fit'; completed results not observed.
records.nextAction: Manually test with a known machine in a browser.

records.subject: canirun.ai
records.claim: canirun.ai lists per-model quantisation options (Q2_K..Q8_0, F16), context window, task/licence/size filters and sort by score, VRAM, speed; shows an undefined 'AA' score.
records.evidence: Model cards and filter controls in fetched page.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: No published methodology; /about returns 404. Memory breakdown (weights/KV) fields rendered as placeholders; multi-GPU limited to a GPU count display.
records.nextAction: Check whether the KV-cache/weights breakdown populates client-side.

records.subject: canitrun.net
records.claim: canitrun.net is a live LLM (not games) fit checker: ~107 GPU/Mac entries or browser detection, ~114 models, S-F grades, bandwidth-based speed estimates and an Ollama getting-started guide.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: VRAM figures derived from Ollama quant manifests; site states all data is estimated; affiliate links; no context-length, KV-cache, multi-GPU or runtime choice beyond Ollama observed. /get-started URL guessed by TRACE returned 404 (actual path not confirmed).
records.nextAction: Locate the actual install-guide URL from the site navigation.

records.subject: canitrun.net
records.claim: canitrun.net applies a speed penalty when a model spills into CPU offload and weighs speed, VRAM headroom and model quality in its grade.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Formula not published in detail; not copied.

records.subject: canrunai.com
records.claim: canrunai.com is live: pick a GPU and a model to check VRAM, quantisation and context length before downloading; includes GPU/model rankings and finders in EN/ZH/JA.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: No methodology visible; hardware detection, multi-GPU, offload, KV breakdown and runtime suggestions not confirmed from the landing page.
records.nextAction: Inspect a model/GPU result page to confirm breakdown fields.

records.subject: Flavio Copes GPU/VRAM calculator
records.claim: Calculator takes parameter count (with MoE active setting), quant, context length and shows weights + overhead + KV breakdown with formulas and a hardware fit table (Apple tiers at ~72% usable).
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: KV uses a simplified per-1k-token factor ignoring GQA/MLA; multi-GPU not modelled.

records.subject: LLM VRAM and Context Calculator (tools.incoherency.co.uk)
records.claim: Calculator takes layers/KV heads/hidden size, weight and KV precision, context, concurrent sequences, partial GPU offload share, GPU count, per-GPU VRAM and reserve; outputs fit verdict, memory breakdown, and solves backwards for max context/concurrency.
records.evidence: Fetched page inputs and method notes; KV modelled from layers x KV heads x head width x tokens x sequences.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Assumes decoder-only transformer, no activation spikes; no GPU database or runtime suggestions; output rendering not captured.

records.subject: llmfit (AlexsJones/llmfit)
records.claim: llmfit is an MIT-licensed Rust TUI/CLI that detects CPU, RAM, GPU/VRAM (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Apple Silicon) and scores models on memory fit, speed, quality and context; it can bench a running provider.
records.evidence: README (38.3k stars at observation); providers Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Docker Model Runner, LM Studio.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Speed is a bandwidth model; README does not document how multi-GPU VRAM is combined. A secondary guide states NVIDIA VRAM is aggregated across cards, a naive-sum risk.
records.nextAction: Read source to confirm multi-GPU aggregation and KV-cache handling.

records.subject: llmfit
records.claim: Secondary source says llmfit aggregates VRAM across all detected NVIDIA GPUs.
records.evidence: Better Stack guide; not stated in README.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Secondary; may be outdated. Summing VRAM ignores per-card fit and split overheads.

records.subject: Comparator feature pattern
records.claim: Common weakness across fit tools: KV cache is either ignored, flat-percentage overhead, or approximated from parameter count rather than architecture (GQA/MLA/hybrid attention).
records.evidence: Method notes on Flavio Copes (simplified factor) and search-result summaries of BenchLM (flat 15%) and Lillytech (parameter-derived) calculators; canirun.ai breakdown not populated.
records.reproducibility: Synthesis across sources.
records.limitations: BenchLM/Lillytech characterisations come from a search summary, not direct fetches.
records.nextAction: TRACE fit logic should model KV per architecture and per GPU.

records.subject: Comparator feature pattern
records.claim: None of the checked web comparators document multi-GPU split semantics (layer vs tensor), per-GPU fit, mixed-vendor rules, or MoE expert offload; most show at most a GPU count.
records.reproducibility: Synthesis across fetched landing pages.
records.limitations: Based on landing-page text; deeper pages may include more.

records.subject: BaseRT
records.claim: BaseRT exists (basecompute/baseRT): native Metal runtime for Apple Silicon, now also CUDA on NVIDIA GB10/DGX Spark; .base format, Q2-Q8 affine quant with optional AWQ; OpenAI-compatible server with tool calls, continuous batching, paged KV, prefix caching.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Repo Apache-2.0 but prebuilt engine binary is proprietary; no multi-GPU or Intel support.

records.subject: BaseRT
records.claim: Paper claims up to 1.56x decode vs llama.cpp and 1.35x vs MLX on M3/M4 Pro; not yet independently reproduced per a third-party tracker.
records.evidence: Search summary of paper and tracker.
records.reproducibility: Self-reported by the project on its own page; not independently reproduced by TRACE.

records.subject: Berth (T-Crypt/berth)
records.claim: Berth exists: Apache-2.0 Go GPU lease scheduler (alpha v0.3.5) that queues engines (llama.cpp, llama-swap, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, ComfyUI, etc.) for one GPU and waits for driver-reported free memory before granting the next lease.
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.
records.limitations: Release date not shown.

records.subject: Berth
records.claim: Platform support: Linux+NVIDIA supported; Windows+NVIDIA and Linux AMD RDNA3/4 experimental; Intel and Apple 'not supported yet'; multi-GPU experimental as one daemon per card (unified gateway planned v0.4).
records.reproducibility: Re-read the cited page; documentation statement, not a measured result.

records.subject: ByteShape ShapeLearn
records.claim: Quality is reported relative to BF16 across GSM8K, IFEval, MMLU, LiveCodeBench V6, Multi-IF, ACEBench, Multiple HumanEval, BFCL V4, plotted against other public Qwen3.8-27B GGUFs, but numeric scores and sample sizes are only in images.
records.reproducibility: Not extractable as text.
records.relevance: high - coding at equal size (in principle)
records.limitations: No numeric equal-size table; competitors anonymised as bubbles.

records.subject: ByteShape ShapeLearn
records.claim: Throughput on RTX 5090 single stream: 94-119 tok/s plain, 147-164 with MTP, 167-176 with DFlash 2 (requires llama.cpp b10658, 2026-08-27, or newer); 1.28-1.66x (MTP) and 1.34-2.10x (DFlash 2) across six GPUs.
records.reproducibility: Hardware-specific.
records.limitations: Workload-dependent.

records.subject: Coding quality at equal file size (cross-cutting)
records.claim: Of the quant sources reviewed, only GSQ-RCO publishes numeric coding results (LiveCodeBench v6) vs Unsloth at matched size; ByteShape charts coding tasks without numbers; EXL3 uses HumanEval vs bpw on older models; BaseQuant, Unsloth and Tiel rely on KL/top-1 or tiny samples; no source evaluates agentic coding (SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench) per quant.
records.reproducibility: Each component re-checkable.
records.limitations: Absence of agentic per-quant evals is the main evidence gap.
records.nextAction: Consider a TRACE-owned equal-size agentic coding eval (Q4-class: UD-Q4_K_M 16.5 GB vs BaseQuant Medium 16.41 GB).

records.subject: DFlash 2 / DSpark draft models
records.claim: Block-diffusion-style speculative drafts are appearing as official artefacts: KRAFTON Raon-1-mini-preview-dflash2 (0.7B, up to 2.18x), ByteShape DFlash 2 path (1.34-2.10x), Liquid DSpark draft 'coming soon', DeepSeek V4.1 'DSpark speculative decoding'.
records.reproducibility: Vendor speed claims.
records.limitations: DFlash/DSpark methods not researched in this pass.

records.subject: EXL3 (ExLlamaV3)
records.claim: EXL3 is ExLlamaV3's weight format, a QTIP variant (procedural codebook, tail-biting trellis) with different regularisation/packing; single-pass conversion from HF format to any target bitrate; Marlin-inspired GEMM kernels (CUDA); full format spec still pending.
records.reproducibility: Open source; reproducible.
records.limitations: NVIDIA CUDA only in practice; no llama.cpp/Ollama support.
records.nextAction: Confirm current doc path on master.

records.subject: EXL3 (ExLlamaV3)
records.claim: EXL3 evaluation uses wiki2 perplexity vs bpw and vs VRAM, plus HumanEval coding pass rates (Llama 3.1 8B/70B, Llama 3.2 1B, Mistral 7B), with GGUF i-quants described as holding up well; a ~3 bpw HumanEval bump noted as repeatable.
records.reproducibility: Scripts in repo.
records.limitations: Older models only; HumanEval is a weak coding proxy; no current-model (Qwen3.8) comparison.

records.subject: FP8
records.claim: vLLM's quantisation matrix (docs dated 2026-09-14): FP8 W8A8 supported on Ada (SM 8.9), Hopper (SM 9.0) and AMD GPUs; FP8 weight-only via Marlin on Turing*/Ampere/Ada/Hopper; Blackwell not given its own column.
records.reproducibility: Reproducible.
records.limitations: Matrix omits NVFP4/MXFP4 rows and Blackwell column.
records.nextAction: Check ModelOpt / compressed-tensors pages for FP4.

records.subject: FP4 in llama.cpp
records.claim: A community guide reports NVFP4 merged into mainline llama.cpp Mar-Apr 2026 with native Blackwell (sm_120) kernels from build b8967 (2026-04-29); older GPUs load files for memory savings only; it says MXFP4 is only in ik_llama.cpp.
records.reproducibility: Check llama.cpp release notes.
records.limitations: The MXFP4-only-in-ik_llama.cpp statement conflicts with mainline llama.cpp's MXFP4 support added for gpt-oss in Aug 2025 (prior knowledge, not re-verified here).

records.subject: MXFP4
records.claim: MXFP4 (OCP microscaling): 4-bit E2M1 with a power-of-two E8M0 scale per 32 elements (~4.25 bits/value); hardware-native on NVIDIA Blackwell and AMD MI350-class; Hopper runs it via Triton kernels (vLLM gpt-oss) without native FP4 math.
records.reproducibility: Spec-level.
records.limitations: AMD support claim from community sources.

records.subject: NVFP4
records.claim: NVFP4: 4-bit E2M1 values with an FP8 E4M3 scale per 16-element block plus an FP32 per-tensor scale (~4.5 bits/value); natively accelerated by Blackwell 5th-gen Tensor Cores.
records.reproducibility: Spec-level.
records.limitations: Full blog text not retrieved.

records.subject: FP4 portability
records.claim: Official FP4 artefacts in this cohort are vendor-specific: NVFP4 for Raon-1 mini, Muse Spark Open, Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B, Flint, Swift 1.5 (Blackwell-targeted); Kimi K3 ships MXFP4 QAT weights (more portable to AMD); vLLM issue notes no NVIDIA PTQ tool yet emits MXFP4 reaching native FlashInfer MoE kernels.
records.evidence: Synthesis of model cards + runtime issue.
records.reproducibility: Each component checkable.
records.limitations: Hopper/Ada users get no FP4 compute speedup; Apple/CPU need GGUF/MLX.
records.nextAction: Record target hardware alongside every quant recommendation.

records.subject: GSQ-RCO (ISTA DASLab)
records.claim: GSQ (Gumbel-Softmax scalar quantisation) + RCO (budget-constrained per-tensor type allocation) produce standard GGUF; Qwen3.8-27B tiers IQ2_XS 8.4 GB (2.50 bpw), IQ2_S 9.3 GB, IQ3_XXS 10.1 GB, IQ3_S 11.8 GB (3.50 bpw, 'task-lossless'), optional -mtp (+0.35 GB) and BF16 mmproj; imatrix calibration 1000 x 4096 tokens.
records.reproducibility: Re-fetch the primary page; publisher statement, not independently reproduced.
records.limitations: None.

records.subject: GSQ-RCO
records.claim: One of the few equal-size coding comparisons: at ~8.4 GB IQ2_XS beats Unsloth UD-IQ2_S on LiveCodeBench v6 (76.57 vs 72.00), AIME25 and GPQA-D; at ~12 GB IQ3_S beats UD-IQ3_S on LCB v6 (85.71 vs 84.00) but trails on GPQA-D and zero-shot avg; IQ3_S matches BF16 LCB (85.71).
records.evidence: Lab-reported task benchmarks incl. LiveCodeBench v6.
records.reproducibility: Sample sizes/seeds not stated; LCB subset size unknown (85.71 suggests a small item count).
records.relevance: high - coding quality at equal size
records.limitations: Single coding benchmark (no SWE-bench/agentic); unknown seeds; margins within plausible noise at 12 GB.
records.nextAction: Request LCB subset size/seeds; replicate on agentic coding.

records.subject: GSQ paper
records.claim: arXiv:2604.18556 (Dadgarnia, Tabesh, Nikdan, Helcig, Kurtic, Kleinegger, Alistarh; v1 2026-04-20, v2 2026-05-15): GSQ narrows gap to QTIP at 2-3 bits on Llama-3.1-8B/70B, applies to existing GGUF K-quant checkpoints, scales to Kimi-K2.5; abstract names no coding benchmark.
records.reproducibility: Paper + code-dependent.
records.limitations: None.

records.subject: QSpec
records.claim: EMNLP 2025 main (pp. 4779-4795) 'QSpec: Speculative Decoding with Complementary Quantization Schemes' (Zhao, Lu, Wang, Kong, Wu): W4A4-style joint quantisation drafts, weight-only high-precision verifies, sharing weights and KV cache; up to 1.64x over high-precision baselines without quality loss, up to 1.55x over SOTA speculative methods in batched settings.
records.reproducibility: Lossless by construction.
records.limitations: Coding evaluation not stated on landing page.

records.subject: Q-Strata
records.claim: 'Strata' resolves to Q-Strata (arXiv:2608.30564; Lee, Chu, Song; 2026-08-31; EMNLP 2026 main): bi-level mixed-precision bit allocation for MoE LLMs; reports lower WikiText2 perplexity than uniform GPTQ, MxMoE and GEMQ at low bits on Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite.
records.reproducibility: Code reportedly at github.com/snu-mllab/Q-Strata (not verified).
records.limitations: Perplexity only; no coding evaluation; no published GGUF/HF quants of current models found.
records.nextAction: Confirm the task's 'Strata' refers to Q-Strata.

records.subject: SubSpec
records.claim: arXiv:2509.18344 'Speculate Deep and Accurate: Lossless and Training-Free Acceleration for Offloaded LLMs via Substitute Speculative Decoding' (Wang et al.; NeurIPS 2025): low-bit substitute layers for offloaded weights as draft, sharing GPU-resident layers and KV cache; 9.1x for Qwen2.5 7B on MT-Bench (8 GB VRAM), 12.5x average for Qwen2.5 32B (24 GB).
records.reproducibility: Lossless by construction (speculative verification).
records.limitations: Speedups are vs slow offloading baseline, not vs in-VRAM quant; coding tasks not named in abstract.

records.subject: twobit-residual-spec
records.claim: HF repo HappyGuitar123/twobit-residual-spec is MIT research code (not a runtime or model): 2-bit GPTQ+Hadamard draft in VRAM, 6-8-bit residual in system RAM computed on CPU (AVX-512), verifier = draft + residual; scripts target Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma 4 12B/31B.
records.reproducibility: Scripts present; no results published.
records.limitations: No end-to-end speedup, acceptance or accuracy numbers shown; PCIe/CPU residual cost unaddressed; author unverifiable.

records.subject: twobit-residual-spec
records.claim: Conceptually overlaps BitNest (residual-nested draft/target) and SubSpec (offload-aware low-bit draft); no comparison to either is provided.
records.reproducibility: n/a
records.limitations: Interpretation.

records.subject: Unsloth Dynamic GGUF
records.claim: Unsloth Dynamic 3.0 (UD-) GGUFs use imatrix calibration and per-layer mixed types; for Qwen3.8-27B: UD-Q4_K_M 16.5 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 17.6 GB, UD-Q5_K_S/M/XL 18.7/19.8/20.9 GB, UD-Q6_K 22 GB, Q8_0 29 GB (plain 'Q5_K' is not a file name; Q5 comes as K_S/K_M/K_XL).
records.reproducibility: File sizes checkable.
records.limitations: None.

records.subject: Unsloth Dynamic GGUF
records.claim: Unsloth claims Dynamic v3.0 'delivers >10% top-1% better accuracy at the same size compared to every other provider' for Qwen3.8; metric is token-level top-1 agreement / KLD vs BF16 (charts only), no methodology given and no coding benchmark per quant.

records.limitations: Fidelity metric, not task quality; competitors not named.

records.subject: Unsloth NVFP4 (Qwen3.8-27B)
records.claim: Unsloth publishes an NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B for vLLM/SGLang, reporting ~92-97% accuracy recovery vs BF16 (KLD/top-1 by corpus) and ~1.4-1.5x BF16 speed.
